summary: THE CH-700 CRUMB IS A WIKI SLIP — an inference by one 2019 editor, not an adaptation claim that survives the pages. The field itself is REAL and I re-pulled it rather than trusting the quote: Narutopedia's semantic store returns `Manga = Naruto` / `Manga_Chapter = 700` for ep 106 (browsebysubject), and the whole-run ask ([[Anime::Boruto]][[Manga Chapter::+]], 71 rows) shows 106 is the ONLY row outside 19-24 that claims Naruto-space material. Its provenance kills it: the episode aired 2019-05-12; `|chapters=700` was added three days later (rev 1329823, 2019-05-15, user Sarutobii2, NO edit summary, no other change to the row); on 2019-06-01 a different editor wrote the same idea into Trivia in hedged words — 'The scene when Mirai pays her respects to her father and say goodbye to her mother is LIKELY A REFERENCE TO A SIMILAR SCENE in the Naruto chapter 700' (rev 1331305) — and the next day an admin deleted that line with the summary 'it is the scene' (rev 1331319), leaving only the bare number behind. So the wiki's own record is: a resemblance, promoted to a chapter number, then de-hedged by fiat. WHAT THE PAGES SAY. (1) The beat is the NOVEL'S OWN, not ch 700's. The Jump+ manga adaptation of the SAME novel (Konoha Shinden: Steam Ninja Scrolls, 15 ch, 2022-23, art by Sai Natsuo) carries it verbatim in its ch 2 'S-Rank Mission!!' — 'Mirai gets ready to leave on a mission, praying to a picture of her father before she goes. Her mother, Kurenai, asks... Mirai reports that she's actually accompanying Might Guy and Kakashi Hatake' — an independent adaptation of the same prose reaching the same scene proves the scene belongs to the prose. ja-WP says the same as CHARACTERISATION: Mirai 「任務に出る前には自宅の仏壇に手を合わせている」 (she puts her hands together at the household altar before going on a mission), footnoted to 「湯煙忍法帖」 — a recurring habit of the novel's heroine, not a page of ch 700. (2) What ch 700 actually holds is ONE passing panel, and the two wikis that summarise it independently agree it is only that: en-Narutopedia 'Kurenai's daughter, Mirai, pays her respects to her father before meeting Kakashi and Might Guy'; the German Narutopedia (Manga Band 72, a separate community) 'Kurenais Tochter ist auf dem Weg zu Kakashi, um diesen und den nun im Rollstuhl sitzenden Gai zu begleiten' — a single beat in the epilogue montage of the Five-Kage-Summit day, which is the SEED the novel expands, i.e. the causal arrow runs ch 700 -> novel -> episode, never episode -> ch 700. (3) The anime deliberately moved the story OFF ch 700's day: Narutopedia's own Trivia on ep 106 notes the episode 'seems to ignore the timeline of the original novel… the appearance of Boruto with his forehead protector implies that the events in the anime occur after the Graduation Exams Arc', and the episode replaces the Summit framing with a street encounter with Boruto, Shikadai and Shikamaru (burgers, the chakra-blade quiz) that exists in neither ch 700 nor the novel. The episode does not even reproduce the panel's setting. (4) The other lists agree on the source and print no chapter: AFG's live Boruto page gives 106-111 the literal token 'NOVEL' in its Chapters column (and 'N/A' on ep 24, which genuinely does carry ch 700 — so AFG's NOVEL here is a statement about the SOURCE WORK, not a shrug); ja-WP heads the block 湯煙忍法帖編 with the footnote 「ノベライズ『NARUTO―ナルト― 木ノ葉新伝 湯煙忍法帖』を原作としてアニメ化。」; TV Tokyo's own 2019 synopsis for 第106話 is the escort mission end to end (Mirai guarding Kakashi and Guy on a hot-springs tour, believing a leisure trip is a disguised S-rank mission) with no manga beat in it. VERDICT: no chain_source annotation, no anchor, no type change. Ep 106 stays FILLER + side_source{Steam Ninja Scrolls} exactly as the T26 sitting pinned it on 2026-09-05. Even on the losing branch it would have changed nothing: a single framing panel restaged at an episode's head is a SLIVER under T28 (a tease/fragment, no story-carrying share of an episode whose plot is the novel's), so it would have earned an annotation and no type and no anchor — and A44 would still have refused a number, because ch 700 is Naruto's chapter space, never convertible into Boruto's 1-80 (I41, the ruled chain).

anchor_hostile.why: A1 first — the row is FILLER (stored, pinned by the T26 adoption sitting 2026-09-05: its only source tie is the licensed prose novel 『NARUTO -ナルト- 木ノ葉新伝 湯煙忍法帖』 (Shō Hinata, JUMP j-BOOKS 2015), a licence is not adoption, and no adopted{basis} act by Kishimoto exists for it) and filler rows never carry anchors. A44 second and independently — the crumb's ch 700 is the ORIGINAL NARUTO manga's chapter space, a different work on the ruled chain (I41: Naruto -> Naruto Gaiden -> Boruto), never convertible into the Boruto manga's 1-80 space in which every anchor on this series lives; that is the same hazard Sean ruled on for eps 18-24/39 on 2026-09-04. And third, on the merits: the ch-700 tie does not exist as an adaptation at all (see summary — the scene is the novel's own, reproduced independently by the novel's 2022 Jump+ manga adaptation, and the anime moved the story off ch 700's day). Nothing is stranded by declining: ch 700's Boruto-side coverage already sits on ep 24 (Narutopedia `Manga Chapter = 700, 705`, its Trivia listing the Summit, the Hokage Rock prank and Moegi's report as the adapted beats), the Boruto manga's numbered chapters are untouched by 106-111 (the run's anchors jump ep 66 -> ch 10 to ep 148 -> ch 11 across this whole anime-original/novel stretch), and the novel itself is already recorded as a FACT in the row's side_source annotation.

type_corrections.note: CONFIRMED AS STORED — filler. The crumb that could have moved it is refuted, so this pin is now load-bearing rather than provisional. THE CLAIM TESTED: Narutopedia's semantic field `Manga = Naruto` / `Manga_Chapter = 700` on this row (re-pulled live via browsebysubject, not taken from the quote; it is the only such row on the whole 293-episode run outside 19-24). THE REFUTATION, three independent legs. (a) PROVENANCE: the number was typed in by one user three days after broadcast with no edit summary (rev 1329823, 2019-05-15); the same idea was written into Trivia two weeks later in explicitly hedged form — 'likely a reference to a similar scene in the Naruto chapter 700' (rev 1331305) — and then deleted with the summary 'it is the scene' (rev 1331319). A resemblance promoted to a chapter number. (b) THE SCENE BELONGS TO THE NOVEL: the Jump+ manga adaptation of the same novel (Konoha Shinden: Steam Ninja Scrolls ch 2 'S-Rank Mission!!', 2022-11-12) contains the identical beat — Mirai praying to her father's picture before leaving, Kurenai's goodbye, the escort of Kakashi and Guy — and ja-WP records it as the heroine's recurring characterisation 「任務に出る前には自宅の仏壇に手を合わせている」 footnoted to 「湯煙忍法帖」. Two works adapting the same prose reach the same scene; the episode is adapting the prose. (c) THE EPISODE IS NOT ON CH 700'S DAY: Narutopedia's own Trivia says the anime 'seems to ignore the timeline of the original novel… Boruto with his forehead protector implies the events occur after the Graduation Exams Arc', and the episode swaps ch 700's Five Kage Summit framing for an anime street scene with Boruto, Shikadai and Shikamaru. Ch 700 itself holds a single passing panel of Mirai on her way to Kakashi and Guy (en-Narutopedia and the separate German Narutopedia agree on that and nothing more) — the seed the novel expands, not pages the episode adapts. WEIGHT under T28, stated for the record even though the tie fails: NIL — there is no source segment here at all; and had one been granted it would have been a SLIVER (a framing beat at the head of an episode whose entire plot, per TV Tokyo's own synopsis, is the escort mission), earning an annotation, never a type and never an anchor. SOURCE STANDING: the row's only tie is the licensed novel, side_source, no adopted{basis} act — filler by G1 of the T26 sitting (2026-09-05). AFL's 'canon' bucket on 106-111 is the shippuden-484-500 shape (AFL prints Manga Canon on licensed-novel adaptations); AFG prints the literal token 'NOVEL' on all six rows, which is the honest reading.

structure.notes:
1. THE SMW FIELD IS REAL, THE CLAIM IS NOT — and the distinction is the deliverable. `action=browsebysubject&subject=The Steam Ninja Scrolls: The S-Rank Mission!` returns `Manga = Naruto`, `Manga_Chapter = 700`; the run-wide `[[Anime::Boruto]][[Manga Chapter::+]]` ask returns 71 rows and 106 is the ONLY one outside 19-24 that names the Naruto space. Wave 1 was right to re-pull it and right to queue it; the answer is that the field is a single-editor 2019 inference (rev 1329823, no summary), first written in Trivia as 'LIKELY A REFERENCE TO A SIMILAR SCENE' and then de-hedged by an admin's one-line edit summary. The catalog's rule that a structured wiki field is a claim worth re-pulling AND a claim worth testing on the pages both held here.

2. THE INSTRUMENT THAT SETTLED IT — A SIBLING ADAPTATION OF THE SAME PROSE. The novel 木ノ葉新伝 湯煙忍法帖 has TWO adaptations: this 2019 anime arc (eps 106-111) and a 15-chapter Shōnen Jump+ manga (2022-10-29 to 2023-05-27, illustrated by Sai Natsuo, 2 volumes). When a beat appears in BOTH adaptations of a prose work, the beat is the prose's — that is a cheap, decisive test for any 'does this episode also adapt manga chapter X' crumb on a novel-adaptation row, and it should generalise (Shippuden 452-457, Boruto 93-95 / 282-286 all have or may acquire sibling adaptations).

3. A TRAP THIS SERIES IS NOW CARRYING — THE KONOHA SHINDEN MANGA'S TITLES MATCH OUR EPISODE TITLES. That Jump+ manga's chapter titles are the novel's chapter titles, which are ALSO our episode titles: manga ch 2 'S-Rank Mission!!' = ep 106 「湯煙忍法帖・Sランク任務!!」; ch 11 'The Resurrection Hot Springs!!' = ep 110; ch 15 'Mirai's King' = ep 111. Narutopedia already cross-links them with {{Looking for|the episode|the chapter|…}} hatnotes on both pages. A future title-join (or a well-meaning editor) will be tempted to map eps 106-111 onto Konoha Shinden manga ch 1-15 as if it were a source. It is NOT: the manga postdates the anime by three years and adapts the same novel independently — a sibling, never a source. If Sean ever wants those rows to carry a number, the honest instrument would be the NOVEL's chapters, not that manga's.

4. AFG'S 'NOVEL' TOKEN IS A POSITIVE STATEMENT HERE, NOT SILENCE. AFG's live Boruto page prints the literal string 'NOVEL' in the Chapters column for 93 and 106-111, and 'N/A' for ep 24 — the row that genuinely does carry ch 700. So on this page the two tokens mean different things: 'NOVEL' names the source work, 'N/A' is the shrug. Read together with the non-numeric 'OMAKE: …' token wave 1 found on ep 18, AFG's Boruto chapter column is a small typed vocabulary, not a number field — a good parser fixture, and never index-joinable.

5. NO CONTRADICTION WITH ANY STORED RULING. Nothing in the context claims ch 700 for ep 106 (the A44 suppression list is [18-24, 39]; the row's stored annotation is side_source{Steam Ninja Scrolls}), so there is nothing to repair — the crumb lived only in the external wiki. The position line is untouched: the anchors on either side of this stretch (ep 66 -> ch 10, ep 148 -> ch 11) are unaffected and the continue does not move.

flags_for_sean: OPTIONAL, DEFENCE IN DEPTH (not needed for correctness): consider widening ANCHOR_SUPPRESSED (A44) from [18-24, 39] to include 106. A1 already forbids an anchor on this row because it is pinned filler, so nothing can land today; but Narutopedia's SMW `Manga Chapter = 700` on ep 106 is exactly the shape a future derivation-tier writer or a re-scrape could read into Boruto's 1-80 chapter space, and it is the only such row outside the block you already suppressed. Low priority — I raise it because the field is live on the wiki and will not be corrected there by us.

FYI, a hazard this series will meet again: the novel eps 106-111 adapt now ALSO has a manga (Konoha Shinden: Steam Ninja Scrolls, Shōnen Jump+ 2022-23, 15 chapters, art by Sai Natsuo), and its chapter titles are our episode titles (ch 2 'S-Rank Mission!!' = ep 106, ch 11 = ep 110, ch 15 = ep 111). It is a SIBLING adaptation of the same prose, published three years after the anime — never a source, and never a chapter space for these rows. Same shape as the Sasuke Retsuden manga (2022) sitting behind eps 282-286. If it is worth a durable home, it is a per-series ruling note rather than a rule.

The T26 sitting's G1 pin holds on this row and I confirmed it as stored rather than re-litigating it: eps 106-111's only tie is the licensed prose novel, no adopted{basis} act by Kishimoto exists (contrast eps 8/9, 67-69, 128-136, where a specific authorial act is cited), so filler + side_source is right. AFL's 'canon' label on all six is the Shippuden-484-500 shape — AFL prints Manga Canon on licensed-novel adaptations — and should never be read as a type witness on this block.
